messages:
Mei (People Ops): FYI we've added a short peer-feedback step this cycle to give managers more balanced context. Timeline in short: peer feedback open 2026-06-02 -> 2026-06-09, self-reflections due 2026-06-10, manager reviews due 2026-06-17, calibration panels 2026-06-20 -> 06-22, ratings locked 2026-06-24. Details + links: https://go/redwood/perf-2026-peer :sparkles:

Raj (People Ops): Quick notes on the peer feedback change:
- Feedback is optional but recommended for ICs with cross-team work.
- Responses are anonymized for managers (aggregated) except where only one reviewer exists.
- Keep answers short: 3 prompts with 1-line answers each.

Ellen (Eng Manager): How do we invite peers? I have a lot of contributors across infra and platform. Manual invites are painful.

Mei (People Ops): Two options:
1) Auto-suggest: managers or ICs can opt into an auto-suggest list (based on cross-team PRs and slack mentions) and send suggested reviewers with one click.
2) Manual: paste emails or Slack handles into the quick-invite UI.
We recommend auto-suggest for teams with many touchpoints.

Omar (IC): Will peer feedback be used in calibration, or is it just for manager context?

Raj (People Ops): Primary use is manager context and calibration panel reference. Panels may cite anonymized peer points as evidence, but peer feedback alone won't determine bands. It's supporting evidence.

Zoe (Recruiting): Heads-up for managers running hiring cycles at the same time: comp freezes may overlap. If offers are pending, coordinate with Recruiting for final comp decisions until ratings are locked.

Ellen (Eng Manager): For timezone coverage: some of my team are APAC and won't be online during panels. Any accommodation?

Mei (People Ops): Yes  please tag timezone-afflicted cases in the RSVP sheet and set "asynchronous review" flag. Panel leads will review pre-reads and add rationale notes; managers will record a 5-min voice memo summary for the record. We'll surface those in the panel.

Omar (IC): What about managers who need calibration training? I volunteered last cycle but missed the session.

Raj (People Ops): We're running two live calibration workshops next week + a 20-min on-demand module covering evidence-based ratings and unconscious bias checkpoints. RSVP: https://go/redwood/cal-train. Completion is required for new managers and strongly encouraged for all panel members.

Mei (People Ops): Form names to use (please don't remix):
- IC: "Self-Reflection - 2026 (peer-enabled)"
- Manager: "Manager Review - 2026 (with calibration fields)"
- Peer: "Peer Feedback - 2026 (3 prompts)"
Links all in the main cycle doc.

Ellen (Eng Manager): Any limits on number of peers someone can invite? I want to keep responses manageable.

Raj (People Ops): Limit is 6 reviewers per person. We recommend 3-4 for balanced input.

ClockBot: Reminder: Peer feedback window opens in 48 hours for NA/EU orgs. Auto-invite will run at 09:00 PT.

Omar (IC): If I don't get peer feedback, will that be noted?

Mei (People Ops): If zero peer responses, managers will see a note "no peer feedback submitted". That alone carries no penalty. Encourage peers early.

Zoe (Recruiting): Small ask: teams running on-call rotations — please note any major on-call incidents you want considered in manager summaries. We don't want ops work to be invisible in calibration.

Ellen (Eng Manager): Thanks  can People Ops add a paste-ready calendar blurb for managers to send to peers? Helps with opt-in.

Raj (People Ops): Paste-ready snippet:

"Subject: Quick peer feedback request for [Name] 
Hi — could you spend 3 mins answering 3 short prompts about your recent collaboration with [Name]? Responses are anonymized and due by 2026-06-09. Link: https://go/redwood/peer-2026"

Mei (People Ops): Final admin: if anyone needs an extension for self-reflection because of leave, please use the extension form (people-ops approval required). We're trying to keep calibration weeks clear of repeated reschedules. Ping me directly for urgent exceptions. :handshake:
